title: A Custom graph node receives the inbound MIDI the graph already gathered

needles: const CustomNodeEventProcessFn* live_custom_event_processor(NodeId id) const noexcept;

installed_sdk.rationale: core/host/include/pulp/ is installed by the per-subsystem header loop in tools/cmake/PulpInstallRules.cmake, which appends `host` whenever the pulp-host target exists and installs the tree FILES_MATCHING "*.hpp". An SDK consumer therefore gets custom_node_events.hpp, the two new CustomNodeType callbacks and the live_custom_event_processor accessor, and can register an event-aware Custom node against the installed headers. Measured against that loop rather than assumed.

needles: const CustomNodeEventProcessFn* live_custom_event_processor(NodeId id) const noexcept;

offline_timeline_cli.rationale: No CLI verb, flag, or handler changes. A Custom node type is registered from C++ against a SignalGraph; the offline timeline CLI neither registers node types nor reaches this callback.

offline_timeline_mcp.rationale: No MCP tool definition or handler changes, for the same reason as the CLI: there is no MCP surface that registers a CustomNodeType.

live_product_control.rationale: A musician cannot reach this. It is an authoring capability for code that builds a graph, and the route that would expose it in a product is the Forge CustomNodeType pack. That route is blocked earlier than it appears: a pack entry must be lowerable because packs are registered before bake(), while registration here refuses a lowerable event-aware type and the baked binder carries no event binder at all. The bake layer needs an event plane before a pack entry is even expressible, so that is the first dependency rather than the pack itself.

design_time_agent_manifest.rationale: The generated manifest publishes signal.custom-node-events with typed bindings for the event block and the node type, plus operational probes, so an agent reading the installed manifest can discover that a Custom graph node consumes events. The supporting header custom_node_events.hpp is also tracked by the surface now that the reviewed-host table names it and carries its own host domain.
